name: Belgium

authorities.competent_authority: FAMHP (Federal Agency for Medicines and Health Products): Belgian national competent authority. Publishes the List of requested documents in CTIS for Belgium (30 June 2026) and the Belgium CTR dossier requirements (updated 30 June 2026).
authorities.ethics: CT-College (Clinical Trial College): independent college that assigns a recognised ethics committee and coordinates the ethics review; publishes the national ICF templates, guidance and advice. The assigned ethics committee reviews the ICF in one language. BAREC (Belgian Association of Research Ethics Committees) issues joint advice with the CT-College (patient-facing documents, paediatric signatures, pregnancy follow-up, lifting traceability of samples, external recruitment platforms).
authorities.procedure: The sponsor submits one dossier through CTIS and receives the Belgian decision through the same system.
authorities.fee: No proof of fee payment at CTIS submission. Belgium invoices applicable safety follow-up and inspection fees separately (BE-PII-CHECKLIST#not-required).
authorities.law: Belgian Law of 7 May 2017 on clinical trials of medicinal products for human use (consolidated through 4 June 2026); Belgian Patients' Rights Act of 22 August 2002 (Articles 12 and 14, representatives); Law of 7 May 2004 on experiments on the human person (pregnant-partner follow-up, liability and insurance); Belgian human biological material (biobank) legislation.
authorities.insurance: No-fault sponsor liability; insurance required before the trial begins. The certificate states the insured amount and refers to applicable national legislation.

answer_languages_note: Belgium is a three-language country. Each participant language is a package: fr (French), nl (Dutch), de (German). Which packages a trial needs follows from the language region of each site and the intended participants (language_rules; study facts sites.language_regions and population.brussels_language_groups). Participant documents (K2, L1, L1 population variations, L2) are required in every language of the trial's regions and submitted in CTIS in each of them. Administrative documents (K1, M1, M2, N1, O1, P, R1, S1) may be in French, Dutch, German or English; one language version is enough (DECISIONS.md D1). No participant templates were supplied for any language. Per document, languages_required says which languages are needed and when.

language_rules.rule: The application dossier may be in Dutch, French, German or English. Participant information, informed consent forms and recruitment materials must be written in the language or languages of the participants and submitted at least in the official language or languages of the region where the trial will run (BE-HUB, BE-ICF).
language_rules.when_dutch: Dutch (nl) for participants recruited in the Dutch-speaking region (Flanders), and for Dutch-speaking participants at Brussels sites.
language_rules.when_french: French (fr) for participants recruited in the French-speaking region (Wallonia), and for French-speaking participants at Brussels sites.
language_rules.when_german: German (de) for participants recruited in the German-speaking region. The CT-College template package is published in Dutch, French and English only: for recruitment in the German-speaking region confirm the expected implementation of the mandatory template with FAMHP or the CT-College before submission and document the translation approach (DECISIONS.md D4).
language_rules.brussels: Plan French and Dutch versions when both language groups may be recruited; a site-specific recruitment plan may justify the exact set (study fact population.brussels_language_groups; DECISIONS.md D2).
language_rules.translations: The sponsor is responsible for accurate, matching translations, even though the assigned ethics committee reviews the ICF in one language. Use the current CT-College source text for each official language and do not re-translate its standard paragraphs; translate only the study-specific content. Risk frequencies and time periods keep the same meaning across the Dutch, French, German and English versions.
language_rules.privacy_information: Participant-facing privacy information must be available in the same regional languages as the ICF.
language_rules.endpoint_instruments: Endpoint-related participant instruments belong with the protocol in Part I: multinational trials submit only the English version; mono-national trials may submit a Member State language version in Part I when no English version exists (FAMHP list, June 2026).
language_rules.staff_language: External recruitment platforms and call centres use trained staff who speak the participant's language (BAREC and CT-College advice, August 2026).
language_rules.form_answers: Shared EU forms (content/eu/templates/part-ii) are answered in French, Dutch, German or English. Default: the reference package language (DECISIONS.md D1).

study_facts_country_specific.sites.language_regions: In which language region does each Belgian site recruit: Dutch-speaking region (Flanders), French-speaking region (Wallonia), German-speaking region, or the bilingual Brussels-Capital region? Decides the participant languages (nl, fr, de).
study_facts_country_specific.population.brussels_language_groups: For Brussels sites: will French-speaking participants, Dutch-speaking participants or both be recruited (site-specific recruitment plan)?
study_facts_country_specific.trial.vaccine: Is the investigational product a vaccine tested in adult healthy volunteers (CT-College vaccine template, recommended while under revision)?
study_facts_country_specific.recruitment.external_platform: Will an external platform or call centre recruit or prescreen participants (role, privacy policy, staff qualifications, consent and data handling must be documented)?
study_facts_country_specific.recruitment.prescreening_data: Are study-specific prescreening data collected (a signed consent form is required)?
study_facts_country_specific.recruitment.pre_recruitment: Does an early-phase unit use pre-recruitment (volunteer databases or panels) before trial authorisation (CT-College recommendation)?
study_facts_country_specific.trial.multinational: Is the trial multinational (endpoint-related instruments: English version only, in Part I)?
study_facts_country_specific.samples.use_beyond_same_disease_treatmen: Does any proposed use of human biological material go beyond research on the same disease, treatment or drug described in the protocol (Belgian biobank registration required)?
study_facts_country_specific.samples.anonymisation_proposed: Is anonymisation of samples by lifting traceability proposed (explicit consent and a refusal system required)?
study_facts_country_specific.privacy.gdpr_confirmation_in_icf: Does the ICF contain the confirmation that collection and processing comply with the GDPR and national implementing law (if not, a separate R1 statement is needed)?
study_facts_country_specific.compensation.participants: Are participants reimbursed or compensated (EU compensation template, amounts matching the ICF)?
study_facts_country_specific.contract.site_payments_or_agreements: Are there payments to sites or investigators, investigator compensation or other sponsor-site agreements (P.70 and P.71)?
study_facts_country_specific.sites.procedures_at_other_facility: Do trial procedures take place at a facility other than the site (identify the facility and the planned agreement in N1)?
study_facts_country_specific.trial.dental: Is it a dental trial (a dentist may conduct the consent interview)?
study_facts_country_specific.application.type: Initial application, addition of Belgium or substantial modification adding Belgian sites, and the submission date: the EU procedure template, the S1 template and the Statement on financing are mandatory for submissions after 1 January 2025; the CT-College adult ICF templates for new initial applications from 1 August 2025.

template.basis: European Commission combined informed-consent and patient-recruitment procedure template (EudraLex Volume 10); mandatory in Belgium

documents.signature_note: An application document, not a participant-signed form. The guides state no sponsor signature for it.
documents.content: How potential participants are identified, approached, informed, given time to decide and consented, with every special pathway (minors, legal representatives, emergencies, witnesses, electronic consent). Where an external platform or call centre recruits or prescreens: its role, privacy policy, staff qualifications, consent and data handling (BAREC and CT-College advice, endorsed 3 August 2026: site involvement, a clear benefit, trained staff who speak the participant's language, referral to the treating site when appropriate). Study-specific prescreening data require a signed consent form. Healthy-volunteer trials: screening, databases or panels, pre-recruitment (CT-College recommendation), repeat-volunteer controls and the consent interview. Uploaded under K.59 and L.62 (DECISIONS.md D6).

national_fields.v105: Required in Belgium: state that every advertisement and recruitment item is submitted under K.60 in its final wording and presentation, in at least the official language or languages of the region where it is used, and is not promotional and exerts no undue influence. If an external platform or call centre recruits or prescreens (recruitment.external_platform, recruitment.call_centre): describe its role, privacy policy, staff qualifications, consent and data handling, the site's involvement, the clear benefit, trained staff who speak the participant's language and referral to the treating site when appropriate (BAREC and CT-College advice, 3 August 2026); study-specific prescreening data are collected only with a signed consent form. For pre-recruitment by an early-phase unit (recruitment.pre_recruitment): follow the CT-College recommendation (24 January 2025); pre-recruitment does not become trial-specific consent or trial conduct before authorisation; describe databases or panels and repeat-volunteer and safety-database checks.
national_fields.v108: Required in Belgium: the consent interview (Article 29 of Regulation 536/2014) is conducted by a physician (a dentist for a dental trial), who may delegate supporting nursing activities but remains responsible and in control (Law of 7 May 2017); the interview is in person or by video conference, never by telephone alone, and the ICF states which format is used; the participant (or legally designated representative) and the person who conducted the interview sign and date the approved form before any trial-specific procedure; the participant receives a copy. State that the current CT-College ICF template is used for adult patients and adult healthy volunteers (sponsor statement if it is not used or mandatory text is changed) and that participant documents are provided in the official language or languages of each site's region. For electronic consent (consent.electronic): the electronic presentation contains at least the information of the paper ICF, participants can refuse it and use paper, the interview occurs first, the investigator signs last, the signed document is locked with its audit trail preserved and a printed or locked electronic copy is given; a site may refuse electronic information or signing (Belgian guidance on electronic informed consent v2.0, 29 June 2022).
national_fields.v110: Required in Belgium when incapacitated adults are included: the legally designated representative is determined by the Law of 7 May 2017 with Articles 12 and 14 of the Patients' Rights Act, in this order: (1) a representative designated by the adult in a specific written, dated and jointly signed mandate; (2) a court-appointed administrator authorised to exercise the relevant patient rights; (3) a cohabiting spouse, legal cohabitant or de facto cohabiting partner; (4) in order, an adult child, a parent or an adult sibling; (5) if nobody acts or representatives conflict, the healthcare professional safeguards the patient's interests, where appropriate through multidisciplinary consultation. Describe how authority is confirmed and documented, how capacity is assessed and reassessed (diagnosis, disability, temporary confusion or supported communication do not by themselves remove capacity), the adapted information to the participant, how a prior refusal and an explicit objection are respected, and the participant's own consent without undue delay once capable.
national_fields.v114: Required in Belgium when minors are included: the legally designated representative is the person exercising parental authority or the legal guardian (Law of 7 May 2017, Article 11; Patients' Rights Act, Article 12). The parent ICF carries two parent signature lines and both parents' written consent is sought (BAREC and CT-College advice v3.0, 10 July 2026); signing need not be simultaneous. Describe the single-parent exception (other parent deceased, incarcerated, unreachable or truly estranged with no indication of disagreement; not mere absence, separation or divorce), the reasonable efforts to involve both parents, asking the signing parent whether the other agrees, documenting whether the parent signs personally or on behalf of both and the justification; a known refusal by the other parent means no enrolment. Belgium sets no numerical assent age: the investigator assesses discernment case by case (age, maturity, impact of the intervention, mental state, personality, family and social environment, education) and actively seeks and documents assent or dissent; a capable minor's refusal or wish to withdraw is respected. Describe the age-adapted documents planned, renewed assent as understanding develops, and the participant's own consent on reaching 18.
national_fields.v117: Required in Belgium when an impartial witness may be used: only for a participant who can decide but cannot write, after supporting the participant's own communication (accessible formats, assistive technology, reading aloud, an authorised alternative mark); not for a language difference, which needs information in a language the participant understands and a competent interpreter. Describe how the witness's independence is checked and documented (an adult independent of the trial, not part of the investigator team, not controlled by the sponsor, not financially dependent on enrolment, not the substitute decision-maker); justify any relative or support person proposed. The physician (or dentist) conducts the interview and confirms capacity; the method used to record the participant's consent is documented; the witness signs and dates the attestation after observing the process; the interviewer signs and dates the ICF; the participant receives a signed and dated copy in an accessible form; the site keeps the original and documentation of the witness's identity and independence (Law of 7 May 2017, Article 12/1).
national_fields.v121: Required in Belgium when emergency enrolment is used: every Article 35 condition (sudden life-threatening or other sudden serious condition; no prior information or consent possible; no legally designated representative available within the therapeutic window; no known prior objection; scientific grounds for direct clinically relevant benefit; minimal risk and burden compared with standard treatment) and the defined therapeutic window. Describe the emergency trigger, capacity assessment, search for a representative under the Belgian hierarchy, check for prior objections, eligibility decision, the initial intervention and who decided, notification, and later information and consent without undue delay (representative when available first; the participant's own decision once capable); refusal stops further trial interventions; the minor safeguards of Article 32 apply where minors may be enrolled. Emergency clinical care is kept separate from the research intervention, and no form is written as if consent preceded enrolment.

documents.drafting_notes_fr: Partie II CTIS, annexe I K.59 et L.62 (même fichier téléversé aux deux endroits, DECISIONS.md D6). Obligatoire pour toute nouvelle demande initiale ou ajout de la Belgique soumis après le 1er janvier 2025 : modèle UE combiné de procédure de recrutement et de consentement éclairé. Document de demande, sans signature à la soumission. Rédiger en français, néerlandais, allemand ou anglais (langue de réponse : D1). Décrire l'identification, l'approche, l'information, le délai de réflexion et le consentement, avec chaque voie particulière prévue (mineurs, représentants légaux, urgence, témoin impartial, consentement électronique) ; les autres sections sont cochées « Non » et marquées sans objet. Ajouts nationaux dans v105, v108, v110, v114, v117 et v121 (national_fields) : entretien par un médecin (dentiste pour un essai dentaire), en présentiel ou par vidéoconférence et jamais par téléphone seul, hiérarchie belge des représentants, deux lignes de signature parentale, absence d'âge légal d'assentiment, plateformes de recrutement externes et pré-sélection.
documents.drafting_notes_nl: CTIS deel II, bijlage I K.59 en L.62 (hetzelfde bestand op beide plaatsen opgeladen, DECISIONS.md D6). Verplicht voor elke nieuwe initiële aanvraag of toevoeging van België ingediend na 1 januari 2025: het gecombineerde EU-sjabloon voor de rekrutering- en informed-consentprocedure. Aanvraagdocument, geen handtekening bij indiening. In het Nederlands, Frans, Duits of Engels (antwoordtaal: D1). Beschrijf identificatie, benadering, informatie, bedenktijd en toestemming, met elke bijzondere route in het plan (minderjarigen, wettelijke vertegenwoordigers, noodsituatie, onpartijdige getuige, elektronische toestemming); de overige secties krijgen 'Nee' en niet van toepassing. Nationale aanvullingen in v105, v108, v110, v114, v117 en v121 (national_fields): gesprek door een arts (tandarts bij een tandheelkundige studie), persoonlijk of via videoconferentie en nooit alleen telefonisch, Belgische hiërarchie van vertegenwoordigers, twee handtekeninglijnen voor ouders, geen wettelijke leeftijd voor assent, externe rekruteringsplatformen en prescreening.
documents.drafting_notes_de: CTIS Teil II, Anhang I K.59 und L.62 (dieselbe Datei an beiden Stellen hochgeladen, DECISIONS.md D6). Pflicht für jeden neuen Erstantrag oder jede Hinzufügung Belgiens nach dem 1. Januar 2025: kombinierte EU-Vorlage für das Rekrutierungs- und Einwilligungsverfahren. Antragsdokument, keine Unterschrift bei Einreichung. Auf Deutsch, Französisch, Niederländisch oder Englisch (Antwortsprache: D1). Identifizierung, Ansprache, Aufklärung, Bedenkzeit und Einwilligung beschreiben, mit jedem geplanten besonderen Weg (Minderjährige, gesetzliche Vertreter, Notfall, unparteiischer Zeuge, elektronische Einwilligung); übrige Abschnitte mit 'Nein' und nicht zutreffend. Nationale Ergänzungen in v105, v108, v110, v114, v117 und v121 (national_fields): Aufklärungsgespräch durch einen Arzt (Zahnarzt bei zahnmedizinischen Prüfungen), persönlich oder per Videokonferenz, nie nur telefonisch, belgische Vertreterrangfolge, zwei Unterschriftszeilen für Eltern, kein gesetzliches Zustimmungsalter, externe Rekrutierungsplattformen und Vorauswahl.

documents.trigger_text: Every advertisement or recruitment item that will be used (including website text, call scripts and other material used to attract volunteers). If none is used, no item is required.
documents.language_rule: At least the official language or languages of the region where the item will be used.

languages_required.fr: Required, and submitted in CTIS, when participants are recruited in the French-speaking region (Wallonia) or French-speaking participants are recruited at a Brussels site (sites.language_regions, population.brussels_language_groups).
languages_required.nl: Required, and submitted in CTIS, when participants are recruited in the Dutch-speaking region (Flanders) or Dutch-speaking participants are recruited at a Brussels site (sites.language_regions, population.brussels_language_groups).
languages_required.de: Required, and submitted in CTIS, when participants are recruited in the German-speaking region (sites.language_regions). documents.content: Final wording and presentation as it will be used. Not promotional and no undue influence; compensation disclosed clearly, without presenting payment as a reason to ignore risk (healthy volunteers). BAREC's list of documents needing no ethics review does not exempt recruitment advertising.
documents.drafting_notes_fr: Partie II CTIS, annexe I K.60. Conditionnel : chaque annonce ou support de recrutement utilisé (y compris textes de site web et scripts d'appel). Au moins dans la ou les langues officielles de la région où il est utilisé ; version soumise avec le texte et la présentation définitifs. Pas de contenu promotionnel ni d'influence indue ; indemnisation présentée clairement, sans en faire une raison d'accepter un risque. Pas de signature.
documents.drafting_notes_nl: CTIS deel II, bijlage I K.60. Voorwaardelijk: elke advertentie of elk rekruteringsmateriaal dat gebruikt wordt (ook websiteteksten en belscripts). Minstens in de officiële taal of talen van de regio waar het gebruikt wordt; de ingediende versie toont de definitieve tekst en vormgeving. Niet promotioneel en geen ongepaste beïnvloeding; vergoeding duidelijk vermeld, zonder ze voor te stellen als reden om een risico te aanvaarden. Geen handtekening.
documents.drafting_notes_de: CTIS Teil II, Anhang I K.60. Bedingt: jede verwendete Anzeige und jedes Rekrutierungsmaterial (auch Webseitentexte und Anrufskripte). Mindestens in der Amtssprache oder den Amtssprachen der Region, in der es verwendet wird; die eingereichte Fassung zeigt den endgültigen Text und die endgültige Gestaltung. Nicht werblich und ohne unzulässige Beeinflussung; Vergütung klar angegeben, ohne sie als Grund darzustellen, ein Risiko in Kauf zu nehmen. Keine Unterschrift.

documents.content: Each blank PIS/ICF for the main adult population, on the current CT-College template: fixed text and structure preserved; study-specific title, purpose, design, procedures, visits, investigational treatment, risks, reproductive precautions, benefits, alternatives, costs, compensation, insurance, privacy, samples and contacts inserted where directed; template instructions followed where a topic does not apply. Signed and dated at consent by the participant and by the physician who conducted the interview (blank in CTIS). Includes the GDPR confirmation unless a separate R1 statement is filed.
documents.drafting_notes_fr: Partie II CTIS, annexe I L.61 et L.63. Obligatoire, un jeu par population, dans chaque langue requise par les régions des sites. Modèle CT-College obligatoire pour les nouvelles demandes initiales d'essais interventionnels avec médicament chez des patients adultes (mis à jour le 4 juin 2026) ou des volontaires sains adultes (22 juillet 2026) soumises à partir du 1er août 2025 : conserver le texte standard et la structure, utiliser le texte source CT-College de chaque langue officielle et ne traduire que le contenu propre à l'étude. Déclaration du promoteur du paquet de modèles si le modèle n'est pas utilisé ou si un texte obligatoire est modifié. Formulaire vierge et non signé dans CTIS ; signatures et dates du participant et du médecin ayant mené l'entretien au moment du consentement. Inclure la confirmation RGPD (sinon R1). Aucun modèle fourni (DECISIONS.md D5).
documents.drafting_notes_nl: CTIS deel II, bijlage I L.61 en L.63. Verplicht, één set per populatie, in elke taal die de regio's van de sites vereisen. CT-College-sjabloon verplicht voor nieuwe initiële aanvragen van interventionele geneesmiddelenstudies bij volwassen patiënten (bijgewerkt 4 juni 2026) of gezonde volwassen deelnemers (22 juli 2026) ingediend vanaf 1 augustus 2025: standaardtekst en structuur behouden, de CT-College-brontekst van elke officiële taal gebruiken en alleen studiespecifieke inhoud vertalen. Sponsorverklaring uit het sjabloonpakket als het sjabloon niet gebruikt wordt of verplichte tekst gewijzigd wordt. Leeg en ongetekend in CTIS; handtekening en datum van de deelnemer en van de arts die het gesprek voerde bij de toestemming. AVG-bevestiging opnemen (anders R1). Geen sjabloon aangeleverd (DECISIONS.md D5).
documents.drafting_notes_de: CTIS Teil II, Anhang I L.61 und L.63. Pflicht, ein Satz je Population, in jeder Sprache, die die Regionen der Prüfstellen verlangen. CT-College-Vorlage Pflicht für neue Erstanträge interventioneller Arzneimittelprüfungen bei erwachsenen Patienten (aktualisiert 4. Juni 2026) oder gesunden Erwachsenen (22. Juli 2026), eingereicht ab 1. August 2025: Standardtext und Struktur beibehalten, nur studienspezifische Inhalte übersetzen. Die Vorlage liegt nicht auf Deutsch vor: Umsetzung mit FAMHP oder CT-College klären und das Übersetzungsvorgehen dokumentieren (D4). Sponsorerklärung aus dem Vorlagenpaket, wenn die Vorlage nicht verwendet oder Pflichttext geändert wird. Leer und ohne Unterschrift in CTIS; Unterschrift und Datum der Teilnehmerin oder des Teilnehmers und des Arztes, der das Gespräch geführt hat, bei der Einwilligung. DSGVO-Bestätigung aufnehmen (sonst R1). Keine Vorlage geliefert (DECISIONS.md D5).

documents.content: Separate or clearly adapted document sets whenever the consent logic changes (BE-ICF): healthy-volunteer ICF (CT-College, mandatory; vaccine template recommended), parent/guardian ICF with two parent signature lines plus age-adapted child and adolescent information or assent, legally designated representative ICF plus adapted participant information, emergency subsequent-consent forms for participant and representative, witness signature page, pregnancy follow-up, infant authorisation and pregnant-partner ICF, optional future use and anonymisation consent. All blank at submission.
documents.drafting_notes_fr: Partie II CTIS, annexe I L.61 et L.63. Conditionnel : documents séparés ou adaptés dès qu'une population ne peut pas utiliser le formulaire standard pour patients adultes (volontaires sains, mineurs, adultes incapables, urgence, participant ne pouvant pas écrire, suivi de grossesse, utilisation future facultative). Même règle linguistique régionale que le formulaire principal. Volontaires sains : modèle CT-College obligatoire (vaccins : modèle recommandé). Mineurs : deux lignes de signature parentale, information adaptée à l'âge sans tranches d'âge légales. Choix facultatifs séparés de la décision principale. Formulaires vierges à la soumission. Aucun modèle fourni.
documents.drafting_notes_nl: CTIS deel II, bijlage I L.61 en L.63. Voorwaardelijk: aparte of aangepaste documenten zodra een populatie het standaardformulier voor volwassen patiënten niet ongewijzigd kan gebruiken (gezonde vrijwilligers, minderjarigen, wilsonbekwame volwassenen, noodsituatie, deelnemer die niet kan schrijven, zwangerschapsopvolging, optioneel toekomstig gebruik). Zelfde regionale taalregel als het hoofdformulier. Gezonde vrijwilligers: CT-College-sjabloon verplicht (vaccins: sjabloon aanbevolen). Minderjarigen: twee handtekeninglijnen voor ouders, leeftijdsaangepaste informatie zonder wettelijke leeftijdsgroepen. Optionele keuzes los van de hoofdbeslissing. Lege formulieren bij indiening. documents.drafting_notes_de: CTIS Teil II, Abschnitt O. Pflicht. Artikel 12 des Gesetzes vom 7. Mai 2017 muss nicht ausdrücklich genannt werden, die Deckung muss aber zur belgischen Prüfung passen. Übereinstimmung mit den Einwilligungsformularen prüfen.

documents.content: Payments to participants: reimbursement of expenses distinguished from compensation for time, inconvenience or burden; amounts, schedule, deductions after withdrawal and non-cash benefits. Amounts and payment conditions match the ICF and the Belgian financing statement. Healthy volunteers: compensation linked to time and burden, not to successful completion or tolerance of risk; withdrawal does not cause disproportionate financial loss (CT-College guidance on compensation, 20 April 2026).
documents.drafting_notes_fr: Partie II CTIS, annexe I P.70. Conditionnel : remboursement ou indemnisation des participants, décrit avec le modèle UE. Distinguer le remboursement des frais de l'indemnisation du temps, des désagréments ou de la charge ; montants, calendrier, retenues en cas de retrait et avantages non monétaires, identiques au formulaire de consentement et à la déclaration de financement. Volontaires sains : indemnisation liée au temps et à la charge, jamais à l'achèvement ou à l'acceptation du risque. Montants fournis par le promoteur, jamais inventés.
documents.drafting_notes_nl: CTIS deel II, bijlage I P.70. Voorwaardelijk: terugbetaling of vergoeding van deelnemers, beschreven met het EU-sjabloon. Onderscheid terugbetaling van kosten van vergoeding voor tijd, ongemak of belasting; bedragen, schema, inhoudingen bij terugtrekking en niet-financiële voordelen, gelijk aan het toestemmingsformulier en de financieringsverklaring. Gezonde vrijwilligers: vergoeding gekoppeld aan tijd en belasting, nooit aan voltooiing of het aanvaarden van risico. Bedragen komen van de sponsor, nooit verzonnen.
documents.drafting_notes_de: CTIS Teil II, Anhang I P.70. Bedingt: Erstattung oder Vergütung der Teilnehmenden, beschrieben mit der EU-Vorlage. Erstattung von Auslagen von der Vergütung für Zeit, Unannehmlichkeiten oder Belastung trennen; Beträge, Zeitplan, Abzüge bei Rückzug und nicht-monetäre Leistungen, übereinstimmend mit dem Einwilligungsformular und der Finanzierungserklärung. Gesunde Freiwillige: Vergütung nach Zeit und Belastung, nie nach Abschluss oder Hinnahme von Risiken. Beträge vom Sponsor, nie erfunden.

documents.content: Sample collection, archive use, analysis, storage, access, coding and future use, consistent with the protocol, laboratory manual and ICFs. Section 5.1 carries the prescribed Belgian text and the scope declaration: all use limited to research on the same disease, treatment or drug described in the protocol, or research beyond that scope, in which case the material falls under Belgian biobank legislation and is registered in a Belgian biobank. Anonymisation by lifting traceability needs explicit consent and a refusal system.

national_fields.f03: Required in Belgium (section 5.1): insert the prescribed Belgian text (not given in the guides and not supplied: leave the instruction and raise missing data until it is supplied, DECISIONS.md D15) and select one scope position: (a) all use described in the protocol is limited to research involving the same disease, treatment or drug; or (b) the protocol includes research beyond that scope, so the relevant material falls under Belgian biobank legislation and will be registered in a Belgian biobank (name it). Justify the classification (for example, minor modifications of the same drug may stay within the same-drug concept; breast cancer research does not cover all cancers). When anonymisation by lifting traceability is proposed: explicit consent of the living donor, explanation of the rights lost, and a system that prevents anonymisation when consent was refused (BAREC and CT-College, 14 November 2025).

documents.drafting_notes_fr: Partie II CTIS, section S. Conditionnel : dès que l'essai collecte, conserve ou propose une utilisation future de matériel biologique humain ; modèle UE obligatoire pour les nouvelles demandes initiales et ajouts de la Belgique soumis après le 1er janvier 2025. Section 5.1 : texte belge prescrit (non fourni, D15) et choix de la portée : même maladie, même traitement ou même médicament, ou au-delà, auquel cas enregistrement dans une biobanque belge. Anonymisation par levée de la traçabilité : consentement explicite et système empêchant l'anonymisation en cas de refus. Concordance avec le protocole, le manuel de laboratoire et les formulaires de consentement.
documents.drafting_notes_nl: CTIS deel II, sectie S. Voorwaardelijk: zodra de studie menselijk lichaamsmateriaal verzamelt, bewaart of toekomstig gebruik voorstelt; EU-sjabloon verplicht voor nieuwe initiële aanvragen en toevoegingen van België ingediend na 1 januari 2025. Sectie 5.1: de voorgeschreven Belgische tekst (niet aangeleverd, D15) en de keuze van de reikwijdte: dezelfde ziekte, behandeling of hetzelfde geneesmiddel, of daarbuiten, met registratie in een Belgische biobank. Anonimisering door het opheffen van de traceerbaarheid: uitdrukkelijke toestemming en een systeem dat anonimisering bij weigering verhindert. Overeenstemming met protocol, labhandboek en toestemmingsformulieren.
documents.drafting_notes_de: CTIS Teil II, Abschnitt S. Bedingt: sobald die Prüfung menschliches biologisches Material erhebt, lagert oder eine künftige Verwendung vorschlägt; EU-Vorlage Pflicht für neue Erstanträge und Hinzufügungen Belgiens nach dem 1. Januar 2025. Abschnitt 5.1: vorgeschriebener belgischer Text (nicht geliefert, D15) und Wahl des Umfangs: dieselbe Krankheit, Behandlung oder dasselbe Arzneimittel, oder darüber hinaus, dann Registrierung in einer belgischen Biobank. Anonymisierung durch Aufhebung der Rückverfolgbarkeit: ausdrückliche Einwilligung und ein System, das die Anonymisierung bei Ablehnung verhindert. Übereinstimmung mit Prüfplan, Laborhandbuch und Einwilligungsformularen.

fields.v105: Required in Belgium: state that every advertisement and recruitment item is submitted under K.60 in its final wording and presentation, in at least the official language or languages of the region where it is used, and is not promotional and exerts no undue influence. If an external platform or call centre recruits or prescreens (recruitment.external_platform, recruitment.call_centre): describe its role, privacy policy, staff qualifications, consent and data handling, the site's involvement, the clear benefit, trained staff who speak the participant's language and referral to the treating site when appropriate (BAREC and CT-College advice, 3 August 2026); study-specific prescreening data are collected only with a signed consent form. For pre-recruitment by an early-phase unit (recruitment.pre_recruitment): follow the CT-College recommendation (24 January 2025); pre-recruitment does not become trial-specific consent or trial conduct before authorisation; describe databases or panels and repeat-volunteer and safety-database checks.
fields.v108: Required in Belgium: the consent interview (Article 29 of Regulation 536/2014) is conducted by a physician (a dentist for a dental trial), who may delegate supporting nursing activities but remains responsible and in control (Law of 7 May 2017); the interview is in person or by video conference, never by telephone alone, and the ICF states which format is used; the participant (or legally designated representative) and the person who conducted the interview sign and date the approved form before any trial-specific procedure; the participant receives a copy. State that the current CT-College ICF template is used for adult patients and adult healthy volunteers (sponsor statement if it is not used or mandatory text is changed) and that participant documents are provided in the official language or languages of each site's region. For electronic consent (consent.electronic): the electronic presentation contains at least the information of the paper ICF, participants can refuse it and use paper, the interview occurs first, the investigator signs last, the signed document is locked with its audit trail preserved and a printed or locked electronic copy is given; a site may refuse electronic information or signing (Belgian guidance on electronic informed consent v2.0, 29 June 2022).
fields.v110: Required in Belgium when incapacitated adults are included: the legally designated representative is determined by the Law of 7 May 2017 with Articles 12 and 14 of the Patients' Rights Act, in this order: (1) a representative designated by the adult in a specific written, dated and jointly signed mandate; (2) a court-appointed administrator authorised to exercise the relevant patient rights; (3) a cohabiting spouse, legal cohabitant or de facto cohabiting partner; (4) in order, an adult child, a parent or an adult sibling; (5) if nobody acts or representatives conflict, the healthcare professional safeguards the patient's interests, where appropriate through multidisciplinary consultation. Describe how authority is confirmed and documented, how capacity is assessed and reassessed (diagnosis, disability, temporary confusion or supported communication do not by themselves remove capacity), the adapted information to the participant, how a prior refusal and an explicit objection are respected, and the participant's own consent without undue delay once capable.
fields.v114: Required in Belgium when minors are included: the legally designated representative is the person exercising parental authority or the legal guardian (Law of 7 May 2017, Article 11; Patients' Rights Act, Article 12). The parent ICF carries two parent signature lines and both parents' written consent is sought (BAREC and CT-College advice v3.0, 10 July 2026); signing need not be simultaneous. Describe the single-parent exception (other parent deceased, incarcerated, unreachable or truly estranged with no indication of disagreement; not mere absence, separation or divorce), the reasonable efforts to involve both parents, asking the signing parent whether the other agrees, documenting whether the parent signs personally or on behalf of both and the justification; a known refusal by the other parent means no enrolment. Belgium sets no numerical assent age: the investigator assesses discernment case by case (age, maturity, impact of the intervention, mental state, personality, family and social environment, education) and actively seeks and documents assent or dissent; a capable minor's refusal or wish to withdraw is respected. Describe the age-adapted documents planned, renewed assent as understanding develops, and the participant's own consent on reaching 18.
fields.v117: Required in Belgium when an impartial witness may be used: only for a participant who can decide but cannot write, after supporting the participant's own communication (accessible formats, assistive technology, reading aloud, an authorised alternative mark); not for a language difference, which needs information in a language the participant understands and a competent interpreter. Describe how the witness's independence is checked and documented (an adult independent of the trial, not part of the investigator team, not controlled by the sponsor, not financially dependent on enrolment, not the substitute decision-maker); justify any relative or support person proposed. The physician (or dentist) conducts the interview and confirms capacity; the method used to record the participant's consent is documented; the witness signs and dates the attestation after observing the process; the interviewer signs and dates the ICF; the participant receives a signed and dated copy in an accessible form; the site keeps the original and documentation of the witness's identity and independence (Law of 7 May 2017, Article 12/1).
fields.v121: Required in Belgium when emergency enrolment is used: every Article 35 condition (sudden life-threatening or other sudden serious condition; no prior information or consent possible; no legally designated representative available within the therapeutic window; no known prior objection; scientific grounds for direct clinically relevant benefit; minimal risk and burden compared with standard treatment) and the defined therapeutic window. Describe the emergency trigger, capacity assessment, search for a representative under the Belgian hierarchy, check for prior objections, eligibility decision, the initial intervention and who decided, notification, and later information and consent without undue delay (representative when available first; the participant's own decision once capable); refusal stops further trial interventions; the minor safeguards of Article 32 apply where minors may be enrolled. Emergency clinical care is kept separate from the research intervention, and no form is written as if consent preceded enrolment.

population_sets.basis: CT-College Model ICF for adult patients (updated 4 June 2026), mandatory for new initial interventional medicinal-product trials submitted from 1 August 2025.
population_sets.note: Preserve the fixed text and structure; translate only study-specific content; sponsor statement if the template is not used or mandatory wording changes. The pregnancy section of the template carries pregnant-participant follow-up information (pregnancy_participant).

population_sets.basis: CT-College Model ICF for healthy adult participants (updated 22 July 2026), mandatory for new initial applications from 1 August 2025.
population_sets.note: Participants enrolled because they are healthy; the protocol's population definition controls. No therapeutic benefit expected; first-in-human uncertainty; confinement, fasting, restrictions, challenge procedures, washouts; incidental findings; precise prohibited substances; compensation linked to time and burden; transparent withdrawal and early-termination payment rules. Do not use the adult-patient template because the product may eventually treat a disease.

population_sets.basis: CT-College Model ICF for vaccine trials in adult healthy volunteers (updated 22 July 2026): recommended, not mandatory, while under revision; strongly recommended to avoid ethics questions.
population_sets.note: The general healthy-volunteer template does not silently replace the vaccine route.

Parent/guardian ICF mandatory, with two parent signature lines. Age-adapted child and adolescent information or assent forms are conditional on the enrolled ages and maturity levels; groups are defined by the protocol and consent procedure, not by national bands (<age group> is the protocol's group). Re-consent at 18 with the adult template (main, healthy or vaccine).

Both mandatory: full representative ICF and information adapted to the participant (simplified sheet, supported communication or the main ICF explained accessibly). Participant's own consent (adult template) once capable.
Both mandatory. Conditional: age-appropriate and parent or guardian pathway (minors templates) if minors may be enrolled. Optional future use is not bundled into deferred consent.

The standard participant ICF in the participant's regional language, with the signature page adapted to the alternative method and a witness statement with signature and date fields (participant expression of consent, witness, interviewer).

CT-College prefers the pharmacovigilance privacy information in the main ICF (pregnancy section of the template); a separate letter or ICF may be used (DECISIONS.md D16). No consent is claimed as the GDPR basis for mandatory pharmacovigilance processing (Art. 6(1)(c) and 9(2)(i)).

Mandatory when planned: information alone is not enough. Specific infant authorisation ICF, or an option in the main ICF provided the other parent also has an information and signature route; two parental signatures preferred, with the two-parent exceptions of the minors guide (DECISIONS.md D17).

Mandatory written consent unless the activity is purely product-safety registration under a legal adverse-event reporting obligation. Thorough partner ICF with privacy information and the insurance clause (Law of 7 May 2004). May be submitted by substantial modification when the situation arises; planning it initially is preferable when pregnancy is foreseeable (DECISIONS.md D18). Questionnaires, calls or other research activities make it interventional and need their own ICF.

Optional, separate decision under Article 28(2); separate tick boxes. Biobank registration when use goes beyond the same disease, treatment or drug; explicit consent for irreversible anonymisation. Matches S1 section 5.1.

population_sets_note: population_sets list which templates a kind of population triggers; the actual populations are defined per study (playbook section 2a) and each population gets its own documents. population_rules.language_choice: Each document is prepared in every language its population needs at the trial's sites: nl (Flanders), fr (Wallonia), de (German-speaking region), fr and nl at Brussels sites when both groups may be recruited (language_rules).

adult_patients.note: CT-College adult-patient template mandatory for new initial interventional medicinal-product trials submitted from 1 August 2025.

healthy_volunteers.note: CT-College healthy-adult template mandatory; for vaccines the vaccine template is recommended while under revision. Healthy status does not remove the separate pregnancy, optional sample research or capacity pathways.

minors.age_band_rule: Belgium sets no single statutory assent age and no national age bands. The principal investigator assesses each minor's capacity for discernment case by case (age, maturity, impact of the intervention, mental state, personality, family and social environment, education). Age-adapted documents are based on the actual population: for example a short illustrated explanation for a young child and a fuller assent document for an older child or adolescent, defined in the protocol and consent procedure (DECISIONS.md D19).
minors.representative: The person exercising parental authority or the legal guardian (Law of 7 May 2017; Patients' Rights Act, Article 12). Confirm parental authority or guardianship before consent.
minors.two_parent_rule: Two parent signature lines in the parent ICF and efforts to obtain both parents' written consent (BAREC and CT-College v3.0, 10 July 2026). Signing need not be simultaneous; one parent may take the form to the other, with enough time before enrolment.
minors.single_parent_exception: Only when the other parent is genuinely unavailable (deceased, incarcerated, unreachable, or truly estranged with no indication of disagreement), not because of absence from the visit, separation or divorce; after reasonable efforts to inform and involve both parents and in the child's best interest. Ask whether the other parent agrees; document whether the parent signs personally or on behalf of both, and the justification.
minors.known_refusal: If the investigator knows that the other parent refuses, the child is not enrolled on one signature.
minors.assent_dissent: Assent or dissent actively sought and documented; a capable minor's explicit refusal or wish to withdraw is respected; lack of a signature line is no reason to ignore dissent. Assent is not described as legal consent.
minors.optional_choices: Parent choices for optional research (future sample use, genetic analysis, pregnancy follow-up, substudies) stay distinct from consent to the main trial.
minors.reconsent: Renewed age-appropriate information and assent when understanding develops or documents change; the participant's own consent as soon as possible after reaching 18 (adult template); explain what happens if the new adult refuses.

representative_hierarchy: A representative designated by the adult in a specific written, dated and jointly signed mandate.
A court-appointed administrator authorised to exercise the relevant patient rights.
A cohabiting spouse, legal cohabitant or de facto cohabiting partner.
In order, an adult child, a parent, or an adult sibling.
If nobody in the hierarchy acts, or representatives conflict, the healthcare professional safeguards the patient's interests, where appropriate through multidisciplinary consultation.
adults_without_capacity.note: Capacity is decision-specific and may change; a diagnosis, disability, temporary confusion or supported communication does not automatically remove capacity. A trusted person who merely assists is not automatically the representative. No enrolment after a relevant prior refusal; an explicit objection is respected. Representative consent and participant assent are kept apart; an assent signature is not presented as legal authorisation. Reassessment points and personal re-consent without undue delay once capable. Optional broad future use is not assumed from representative consent to the main trial.

emergency.note: Only when every Article 35 condition is met and the protocol and K1 describe the pathway; not to solve recruitment difficulty or avoidable planning problems. Representative hierarchy as for adults without capacity. The forms explain what already occurred and never read as if consent had preceded enrolment.

impartial_witness.note: Only for a participant who can decide but cannot write; not for a language difference (interpreter and translated documents instead) and not as a substitute for a legally designated representative. The guides do not address a representative who cannot write.

pregnancy.participant: Pharmacovigilance follow-up; privacy information (GDPR Articles 13 and 14) preferably in the main ICF pregnancy section, or a separate letter or ICF (BE-PT-pregnancy-fr, BE-PT-pregnancy-nl, BE-PT-pregnancy-de). No separate consent for processing required by law.
pregnancy.infant: Specific infant authorisation (BE-PT-infant-fr, BE-PT-infant-nl, BE-PT-infant-de) or an option in the main ICF with a route for the other parent; two parental signatures preferred.
pregnancy.partner: Written consent of the pregnant partner (BE-PT-pregnant-partner-fr, BE-PT-pregnant-partner-nl, BE-PT-pregnant-partner-de) unless purely legal safety registration; the participant cannot consent for the partner; the participant's trial care is not conditional on the partner's agreement.
pregnancy.duration: Follow-up duration defined in time in the protocol and justified (preclinical and clinical exposure data, class effects, fetal-development risks, pharmacokinetics).

secondary_use.note: Separate optional consent for use of identifiable or coded data or material outside the protocol; refusal does not prevent participation unless scientifically integral and assessed as such. Minors: parent permission, assent, personal consent at adulthood for continued optional use where required.

population_rules.shareable_note: Templates whose content need not depend on the population; one shared document for several populations may be agreed with the user once the templates exist.
separate_document_rules: Prepare a separate or clearly adapted document set whenever the consent logic changes (BE-ICF).

Do not bury an optional choice in the signature for the main trial; refusing optional future use, genetic testing or child follow-up does not exclude someone from the main trial unless the protocol justifies it.
The parent ICF and the age-adapted minor documents are separate documents.
The representative receives a full ICF; the participant receives adapted information.
Emergency enrolment needs a participant subsequent-consent form and a representative form.
The pregnant partner, the pregnant participant and the born child have separate decisions.
Study-specific prescreening data require a signed consent form.

drafting_rules: Participant documents in the language or languages of the participants and at least the official language or languages of each site's region (nl Flanders, fr Wallonia, de German-speaking region, fr and nl in Brussels as the population requires); each language version has the same meaning, and the sponsor is responsible for translations.

CT-College templates (adult patients, healthy adults; vaccine template recommended) for new initial interventional medicinal-product trials from 1 August 2025: keep fixed text and structure, use the CT-College source text of each official language, translate only study-specific content, follow template instructions where a topic does not apply rather than silently deleting safeguards; sponsor statement with justification when the template is not used or mandatory wording changes. Confirm the template version is current on the day of submission.

The information lets an adult decide without the protocol: purpose and why invited; product, randomisation, placebo and blinding; visits, tests, procedures, duration and follow-up; foreseeable and unknown risks and burdens; no guaranteed benefit and alternatives; pregnancy, contraception, breastfeeding and partner precautions; samples and data, recipients and retention; optional choices separately; confidentiality and coded data; reimbursement, compensation, injury and Belgian no-fault insurance; voluntariness, withdrawal and continued safety follow-up; contacts for trial questions, urgent issues, participant rights and data protection.

Write for the participant: define medical terms, explain probabilities understandably, short sections, risks specific to the intervention, no investigator-facing lists without context. Do not promise benefit or describe an experimental product as safe or effective.
Compensation and reimbursement match the financial documents (P1, financing statement, site agreement); sample wording matches the protocol and S1; insurance wording matches the certificate.

Privacy: distinguish consent to participate from the legal basis for processing; never call coded data anonymous; identify controllers, recipients, retention, international transfer safeguards, rights and their limits, and data-protection contacts; include the GDPR confirmation in the ICF or file R1.

Consent interview by a physician (dentist for a dental trial), in person or by video conference, never telephone alone; the ICF states the format. Blank, unsigned, version-controlled ICFs in CTIS; signature and date fields for every person whose consent, assent, attestation or authorisation is required, left blank.

Electronic consent: at least the paper ICF's information; screens, images, videos and process submitted as seen plus a printable PDF; paper route available; investigator signs last; locked copy for the participant.
Healthy volunteers: no therapeutic benefit; payment linked to time and burden, not completion or tolerance of risk; withdrawal not disproportionately penalised; neutral recruitment claims.
Minors: two parent signature lines; age-adapted information for the actual population, no invented national age bands; assent and dissent documented; re-consent at 18.
Recruitment material and other patient-facing documents: final wording and presentation; not promotional, no undue influence; incentives disclosed.

Version, date, population and language on every item; version and date in CTIS structured data, not the filename; Annex I letter and language in the filename where practical (for example L Main ICF_NL). Remove signatures, personal addresses and other unnecessary personal data from documents for publication. Tracked-change versions with RFI responses and substantial modifications.

No participant templates were supplied: once the CT-College templates and the other population templates are supplied they are split into templates/participant per language (*_BE_fr.json, *_BE_nl.json, *_BE_de.json); until then documents cannot be drafted from a template (DECISIONS.md D5).

Part II templates (DOCX): yellow [INSERT/IF/OTHERWISE/CHOOSE/NOTE: ...] labels; participant templates (JSON, when supplied): italic text, [square-bracket] notes and "..........." gaps. Nothing of either may remain in a final document.

naming.convention: content/playbook/naming.md (CTCG Best Practice Guide: Naming of Documents in CTIS, v3.0, 10 February 2026)
naming.belgium_note: Participant-facing documents and the procedure carry _BE_fr, _BE_nl or _BE_de (ctis_titles per document). The Belgium checklist page uses descriptive names and Annex I item numbers (K.59, K.60, L.61 to L.63, M.65, M.66, P.69 to P.71); the CTCG pattern is used. The K1 procedure is uploaded under K.59 and L.62 (DECISIONS.md D6). P titles: P1 participant compensation (CTCG title), P2 Belgian Statement on financing, P3 site financial arrangements and agreements (DECISIONS.md D10).
naming.filename_rule: FAMHP recommends the Annex I letter and the document language in the filename (for example L Main ICF_NL) and version and date only in CTIS structured data. Filename base without ( ) / , . ; | [ ].
